besluite.fout: English word order (object before the time phrase) and the padding 'van die week' make the sentence wooden.
besluite.rede: Time before object is the natural Afrikaans order, and 'van die week' adds nothing; 'Party' and the contrast with the next sentence about weddings and festivals stay exact.
'die Indiese gemeenskap van die stad Durban' is acceptable Afrikaans, and the proposal drops 'die stad', which tells a Grade 4 reader what Durban is.

besluite.fout: 'n kwart van 'n brood' is a loose rendering of the fixed Afrikaans phrase 'n kwart brood'.
besluite.rede: The idiomatic phrase says the same thing and matches the lesson's own bunny chow glossary entry; 'gewoonlik' is untouched.

besluite.fout: 'wat' can be read as the subject, so the definition can seem to say the language recognises the laws and government.
besluite.rede: The ambiguity is real, but this is a shared glossary definition, so the rewording has to go through the writer for every lesson at once.
